items.title: Add a shared file lock and an atomic store update

goal.title: Add a shared file lock and an atomic store update
criteria: Many concurrent updaters, each with its own store instance, incrementing one value end with exactly the expected total.
An update whose callback fails leaves the file exactly as it was.
The commit lock behaves as before, with its existing tests unchanged and passing.
Every store implementation, including the ignore-filtering wrapper and the test doubles, supports the new operation.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: internal/store/store_test.go (TestUpdate_ConcurrentIncrementsFromSeparateInstancesAreAllKept, added in the diff): 16 goroutines, each with its own NewFileStore over the same root, each doing 25 Update increments on counter.json, asserting the final N is exactly 400 and that only counter.json remains. FileStore.Update (internal/store/store.go, diff hunk at +210) serialises through filelock.Acquire on abs+".lock" and writes via temp file and rename. The test is the only evidence; I did not run it.

internal/store/store_test.go (TestUpdate_FailingCallbackLeavesTheFileUnchanged): the callback returns ([]byte("half-made"), boom); the test asserts ErrorIs boom, the file still reads "original\n", and requireOnlyFiles shows no temp or lock file. In store.go Update, fn's error returns before CreateTemp, so nothing is written. The test is the only evidence; I did not run it.

internal/autocommit/lock_test.go is not in the diff, so its four tests are unchanged. internal/autocommit/lock.go AcquireLock now delegates to filelock.AcquireWithBackoff(path, LockTimeout, LockStale, lockBackoff) and maps *filelock.LockError to the autocommit *LockError with the same Path and Holder. LockError.Error() is untouched (context lines in the diff hunk at line 37), so the "timed out waiting for the commit lock" message is preserved. filelock.go uses the same stale comparison (> stale) and the same backoff doubling capped at 1s as the removed code.

Every type with a Write/Delete pair in the code root now has Update: FileStore (store.go:239), ignoreStore (ignore.go:89, delegates to s.inner.Update), design_test.go recordingWriter (line 650), set_test.go tagBlindStore (line 2058) and deleteRecordingStore (line 2338). A grep for `) Write(path string, content []byte)` found one more type, metadata/close_test.go fakeStore, but it implements only the metadata.StoreReadWriter surface (Read/Write), not store.Writer, so it needs no Update. store_test.go lines 200-208 also assert the interface conformance for FileStore and ignoreStore.

items.title: Keep a usage index in each knowledge store

goal.title: Keep a usage index in each knowledge store
criteria: Recording a discovery or a retrieval adds exactly one to that entry's count, with the time given, and a retrieval keeps the workflow and spec it was given.
An entry written and then rewritten keeps its first creation date and its counts.
An entry that predates the index gains a record with a creation date (from version history when available) and a tracking start of now.
Records for removed entries disappear, and the index never appears as an entry in list, search, tags or the always-applied rules.
Concurrent searches and reads of one entry from several independent instances are all counted, none lost.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: internal/knowledge/usage.go:134-198: RecordDiscoveries and RecordRetrievals call recordEach, which increments l.Count by exactly one per path, sets Last to the given time (at.UTC()), appends an event with that time, and, for retrievals, copies wf.Kind and wf.Spec into the event (lines 166-187). internal/knowledge/usage_test.go:48-88 asserts count 1 after one discovery, the given timestamp in Last and Recent, a retrieval recorded with Workflow 'implement' and the spec, and a retrieval with nil workflow carrying neither.

usage.go:204-227: EnsureRecord leaves an existing record untouched (the only change is to Created, and only when reconcile just met the path with no history date, line 220-224, which is the first-write case). usage_test.go:113-141 writes, records a retrieval and two discoveries, rewrites, calls EnsureRecord again, and asserts Created and TrackedSince remain t1 and counts remain 1 retrieval and 2 discoveries.

usage.go:312-335 reconcile adds a record for every listed file with no record; usage.go:349-361 datedRecord sets Created from the CreatedDater (version history) when it returns a date, else from store Stat ModTime, and sets TrackedSince to the write time 'at'. usage_test.go:147-190 checks the historic entry dated from history (committed), the handmade entry dated from its mtime (modified), and TrackedSince equal to now for both, plus a trigger entry with the mtime date.

Dropping removed entries: usage.go:329-333 in reconcile deletes any record whose path no longer exists; ForgetRecords (usage.go:233-243) deletes named paths. usage_test.go:194-237 covers both. Reserved exclusion: listFiles in set.go:680-705 skips IsReservedPath paths, so List, Tags and AlwaysAppliedEntries (via readCategories) never see the index, lock or temp files; Search skips them explicitly at set.go:231-237; usage.go:101-109 defines the reserved set. usage_test.go:245-315 asserts the index, lock and temp file are absent from List, Search, Tags, AlwaysAppliedEntries and Usage (Usage excludes them via listFiles), and are refused as entry addresses. Note the index file is not returned by Usage either, since it uses listFiles.

Every index change goes through Set.update (usage.go:291-304), which calls src.store.Update. internal/store/store.go:239-247 FileStore.Update takes filelock.Acquire on the index path plus LockSuffix and then does a read-modify-write through a temp file, so the read-modify-write is atomic across processes. usage_test.go:389-432 starts 8 independent Set instances over one directory, each recording one discovery and one retrieval concurrently, and asserts both counts equal 8 and that no lock or temp file remains. The race test on internal/knowledge also passes per the verification summary.

items.title: Record usage from the knowledge commands

goal.title: Record usage from the knowledge commands
criteria: After a search returning an entry, `knowledge usage` shows one more discovery for it at the search's time.

After an entry is read, or loaded as an always-applied rule, it shows one more retrieval. A read that names its spec is attributed to that spec's running workflow even when other workflows run in parallel, and an unnamed read during a single running workflow names that workflow.
The delete command's existence check, the tags and list commands, and other internal reads change no count.
Writing to the index's location through `knowledge write` is refused with a remediation, and the index is not listed or returned as an entry.
A search or read still returns its result, with a warning, when usage cannot be recorded.
Existing entries written before the change can still be searched and read, and gain a creation date with no manual edit.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: cmd/knowledge.go runKnowledgeSearch (diff hunk ~L435-446) calls recordUsage(result, set.RecordDiscoveries(hits, knowledgeNow())) after the search, one discovery per hit. internal/knowledge/usage.go RecordDiscoveries/recordEach (L134-196) increments Discoveries.Count and sets Last to the given time. cmd/knowledge_usage_test.go TestKnowledgeSearch_RecordsADiscoveryPerHit (L89-112) checks the count and time for returned entries and that a non-returned entry gains nothing.

Retrieval recording: cmd/knowledge.go runKnowledgeRead (diff ~L460-476) calls RecordRetrievals with activeWorkflow(input.Spec); always-applied and conventions do the same (~L187, L214). Named-spec attribution: cmd/knowledge_usage.go activeWorkflow (L129-181) returns the single candidate whose Spec equals the named spec, including lane workflows; test TestKnowledgeRead_NamedSpecPicksItsWorkflowAmongParallelRuns (knowledge_usage_test.go L159-185) covers two parallel lanes. Unnamed single-workflow attribution: L177-178, tested by TestKnowledgeRead_NamesTheSingleRunningWorkflow (L143-154). Note: when a named spec has no running workflow, the code falls through to the single-candidate branch and attributes the read to some other running workflow (L159-180, no test); the criterion does not state that case, so it is noted rather than failed.

list and tags use set.List/set.Tags (cmd/knowledge.go L486, L505), which call listFiles and never call the update/Record path (internal/knowledge/set.go L417-470). The delete existence check at cmd/knowledge.go L594-598 uses set.Read, which is untracked (usage is recorded only in the cmd layer). Delete drops the record via ForgetRecords (L162). TestKnowledgeInternalReadsRecordNothing (knowledge_usage_test.go L189-221) asserts zero counts after list, tags, sources, usage and delete.

internal/knowledge/usage.go IsReservedPath (L101-109) covers .usage-index.json, its .lock and .tmp- files. Set.Write, Set.Delete and Set.Read refuse reserved paths (internal/knowledge/set.go L359, L384, L404) via refuseReserved (usage.go L113-121), which gives ErrCodeIndexReserved and a NextAction pointing at 'knowledge usage'. listFiles skips reserved paths (set.go L699-700) and Set.Search drops them (set.go L231), so list, tags, search and conventions never return them. TestKnowledgeIndexPathIsRefusedAndHidden (knowledge_usage_test.go L226-258) covers write, read and delete.

cmd/knowledge_usage.go recordUsage (L94-99) sets result["usage_warning"] on failure and never returns an error. It wraps the search record (knowledge.go ~L440), the read record (~L470) and the write, delete, conventions and always-applied records. Schemas carry usage_warning (knowledge.go diff L9, L19). TestKnowledge_RecordingFailureStillReturnsTheResult (knowledge_usage_test.go L339-360) corrupts the index and checks that read and search still return content or hits plus the warning.

Pre-existing entries are reconciled on the first index write: internal/knowledge/usage.go reconcile (L312-335) adds a record for every listed file, dated from the git history via gitCreatedDater (cmd/knowledge_usage.go L105-120, injected by newKnowledgeSet in cmd/knowledge.go diff ~L93) or else from the file's mtime (datedRecord L349-361). Search and read do not depend on the index. TestKnowledge_PreExistingEntryCarriesOver (knowledge_usage_test.go L286-307) and TestKnowledge_PreExistingEntryIsDatedFromGitHistory (L311-335) cover this. I did not run the tests; the verdict rests on reading the code and test bodies, and the reported verification passes.

goal.title: Add the prune age setting
criteria: A configuration without the key reports an age of 90 days.
A configured age is read and survives being saved and reloaded.
A negative age is refused with a message naming the key and the fix.
Configurations written before the change load without error and without a migration.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: internal/config/config.go: const DefaultKnowledgePruneMaxAgeDays = 90 and KnowledgeConfig.PruneMaxAgeDays() returns it when Prune.MaxAgeDays is 0 (diff hunk @@ -241). config_test.go TestFromYAMLFile_AbsentKnowledgePruneAgeLoadsAsNinety asserts PruneMaxAgeDays() == 90 for a file without the key and for NewDefault().

config.go: KnowledgeConfig gains Prune KnowledgePruneConfig `yaml:"prune,omitempty"` with MaxAgeDays `yaml:"max_age_days,omitempty"`; Config.Knowledge is KnowledgeConfig (config.go:427), and ToYAMLFile (config.go:976) marshals the whole Config. config_test.go TestToYAMLFile_KnowledgePruneAgeRoundTrips loads max_age_days: 30, asserts it is written as 'prune:\n        max_age_days: 30', reloads it and reads 30 back. The schema version stays 4 (asserted in the test).

config.go KnowledgeConfig.Validate (diff @@ -872): when Prune.MaxAgeDays < 0 it returns output.NewError("config_invalid", "knowledge.prune.max_age_days must be a positive number of days, got -1") with Resource 'knowledge.prune.max_age_days' and NextAction 'set knowledge.prune.max_age_days in .spektacular/config.yaml to a positive number of days (or remove the key to use 90)'. Reached via FromYAMLFile -> Config.Validate -> c.Knowledge.Validate (config.go:495, 764). config_test.go TestFromYAMLFile_NegativeKnowledgePruneAgeIsRefused asserts code, message, resource and next action.

The diff touches only internal/config/config.go and config_test.go. schema.go and internal/migrate are unchanged, so CurrentProjectSchema is still 4 and no migration step was added. The new field is optional with omitempty, so an existing file parses with it absent (config.go:515-537 loader unchanged apart from the new field). config_test.go TestFromYAMLFile_AbsentKnowledgePruneAgeLoadsAsNinety loads a current-schema file without the key with NoError. I did not run the tests myself; the reported go test pass is consistent with these tests, and the test code and the code paths I read support the verdicts.

goal.title: Add the knowledge prune command
criteria: With a 30-day age, an entry created 40 days ago and never retrieved is removed, while one retrieved once in that window and one created 10 days ago are kept.
An old entry that searches surfaced but nobody read is removed, and an entry tracked for less than the age is never removed for non-use.
A corrected entry keeps its usage counts, and a removed or deleted entry leaves no record in the index.
A verdict that the store contradicts, a verdict for the wrong entry, or a change without evidence is refused with a remediation.
The instruction for each entry tells the agent to keep an entry stating an unmet standard as current, and to delete only an entry whose subject no longer exists.
A dry run reports the same removals a real run would make and a verdict for every entry, and afterwards every entry and the index are byte-for-byte unchanged.
Prune's own reads, in a real run or a dry run, change no retrieval count.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: internal/knowledge/usage.go PruneCandidates (diff lines 172-195) removes an entry only when now-Created > maxAge, now-TrackedSince >= maxAge and the last retrieval is nil or older than maxAge; a retrieval 5 days ago keeps the entry and a 10-day-old entry fails the Created test. internal/knowledge/usage_test.go:212-240 (TestPruneCandidates_AgeRule) asserts exactly never-read.md (40d) removed, read-once.md (retrieved 5d ago) and young.md (10d) kept. cmd/knowledge_prune_test.go:259-298 checks the same through the command against the on-disk fixture.

usage.go PruneCandidates ignores Discoveries, so surfaced.md (3 discoveries, never read, 40d) is removed (usage_test.go:227, expected at line 237). The TrackedSince check at usage.go:178 (now.Sub(eu.TrackedSince) < maxAge continues) keeps backfilled.md (created 400d ago, tracked 10d) per usage_test.go:228 and cmd/knowledge_prune_test.go:73. cmd/knowledge_prune_test.go:255-298 asserts the removed set and that the surfaced entry's file and index record are gone.

Corrected: cmd/knowledge.go:532-538 runs set.Write then set.EnsureRecord, and internal/knowledge/usage.go EnsureRecord (about line 204) leaves an existing record untouched, so counts survive. Deleted and removed: cmd/knowledge.go:603-610 calls ForgetRecords after delete, and cmd/knowledge_prune.go applyPruneRemovals (lines 440-457) calls ForgetRecords for each removal; usage.go:233-243 deletes the record. cmd/knowledge_prune_test.go:406-427 asserts backfilled.md keeps 2 discoveries and 1 retrieval after correction, and that removed/deleted paths have no index record.

cmd/knowledge_prune.go: wrong entry refused with knowledge_prune_wrong_entry and a NextAction naming the head verdict command (lines 326-332); change without evidence refused with knowledge_prune_evidence_required (lines 340-346); claims the store contradicts refused with knowledge_prune_claim_mismatch for deleted-but-present, corrected-but-absent, corrected-unchanged and current-but-changed (checkPruneClaim, lines 378-436). Each carries WithNextAction. cmd/knowledge_prune_test.go:308-359 exercises every refusal and requirePruneRefusal asserts a non-empty NextAction.

templates/knowledge/prune-entry.md:23 says an entry stating a standard the code has not yet met is **current**, not stale, and that a gap is work to do; line 24 says only an entry whose subject no longer exists is **deleted**. templates/knowledge_prune_template_test.go:41-63 asserts these phrases render in both real and dry-run instructions.

Dry run uses the same PruneCandidates and the same queue as a real run (cmd/knowledge_prune.go:241-247, applyPruneRemovals only when !pruneDryRun). The run file lives in dataDir under .spektacular (line 46, 554-560), outside any store. Usage, List and Read are read-only (internal/knowledge/usage.go:245-284 says Usage writes nothing; set.go:358-377 Read has no recording; set.go:417 List does not call update). checkPruneClaim refuses any change in dry run (cmd/knowledge_prune.go:391-400). cmd/knowledge_prune_test.go:480-547 hashes both stores, including index files, before and after a dry run and asserts the dry-run would_remove set equals a real run's removals. Not verified by running tests; verification summary reports pass.

Prune reads use set.Read, which never records usage (internal/knowledge/set.go:358-377); cmd/knowledge_prune.go:263, 379 and 465 call set.Read directly, and the template forbids the agent from running knowledge read or search (templates/knowledge/prune-entry.md:19). Only RecordRetrievals and EnsureRecord record usage, and prune calls neither on its reads. cmd/knowledge_prune_test.go:551-575 compares retrieval and discovery counts before and after dry and real runs and asserts unchanged values.

items.title: Rewrite the installed instructions to write knowledge, then report it

goal.title: Rewrite the installed instructions to write knowledge, then report it
criteria: The guidance a fresh `init` installs tells agents to write durable knowledge themselves and report it, and no longer tells them to offer it and wait for a decision.
No plan, implement or epic instruction asks the user whether to save knowledge, in standalone or orchestrated runs.
Each instruction tells the agent to name the entry it wrote, its store and path, and why it was worth keeping.
The AGENTS.md knowledge section keeps its heading and stays within the compact-section limits.
The plan discovery step's knowledge reads name the plan's spec.
